inspection_outcome: Four confirmed Major and eight Minor findings; explicit repair boundaries and remaining proof-completeness limitations retained.
summary: Four demonstrated core defects concern the index domain, inversion energy conversion, local-to-global avoidance and the Poincare step in C2 convergence. Eight bounded local corrections remain. Exact source only; energy quantization itself not disproved.

problems.title: Negative-cone span is not Morse index

source_claim.location: p5 equation(1);p8 equation(6);TheoremIII p4 andTheorem4.3 p12
source_claim.claim: Index is dimension of the span of individually strictly negative velocities.

problems.assumptions: Closed smooth genus1 Willmore immersion, normal smooth variations, fixed energy, no umbilics; immersion rather than embedding is allowed.
problems.counterexample: Double-covered Clifford torus Psi=(cosu,sinu,cosv,sinv)/sqrt2, u period4pi,v period2pi. g=diag(1/2,1/2),H0,E8pi². Q_E(f)=integral f(Delta+2)(Delta+4)f, eigenvalues lambda=2(m²/4+n²). Only labels(±1,±1) are negative; ordinary index4. For f=cos(u/2)cosv,Q=−3pi²/4. If Q(v)<0, all w=((v+tw)−v)/t belong to span of negative cone for small t, so printed index is infinite. Stereographic Phi=(cosu,sinu,cosv)/(sqrt2−sinv) gives a real closed R3 example. Smooth time compression realizes every velocity on(-1,1).
problems.counterevidence: Constant sequence still quantizes. Disjoint supports in Section7.3 do produce a true negative-definite span for the corrected index.
problems.impact: The central bounded-index hypothesis formally excludes finite nonzero Morse-index surfaces and reduces to stable sequences; this is a scope change, not a demonstrated false E energy identity.
problems.correction: Define maximal dimension of a subspace on whose every nonzero vector the Hessian is strictly negative, both in(1)and(6).

check.independent_reasoning: Negative-direction span equals the whole admissible vector space as soon as Q(v)<0: v+t w and v are both negative for small t. Root checked the double Clifford cover spectrum2(m^2/4+n^2), exactly four real negative directions with2<lambda<4, and realization of velocities by local immersed variations. The printed central bounded-index domain is thereby reduced, although the constant sequence still quantizes.

problems.title: Mean-curvature gauge cannot avoid every global image under local Willmore assumptions

source_claim.location: Section5.1 p13;Lemma5.2 p14 equations(15)–(16);global avoidance proof p15
source_claim.claim: A topology-preserving Mobius transformation always makes the unweighted annular mean curvature zero, although the closed immersion need only be Willmore on the cylinder.

problems.assumptions: Fixed closed genus1 surface;smooth globally immersed family;uniform whole-surface integral|A|²;nonumbilic conformal Willmore neck;total cylinder curvature arbitrarily small;uniform local strip/dyadic energy tends0.
problems.counterexample: Use explicit Willmore ring torus R=sqrt2, retain an isothermal disk around H≠0. Its annular mean Y determines a smooth nondegenerate round sphere S_rho of all zero-mean inversion poles. Connect-sum outside the retained disk with two labelled coincident copies of S_rho; remove disjoint outer caps so the unchanged spherical pieces still cover all of S_rho. Fixed-radius tubes and smooth collars vary in a compact smooth family, retaining genus1 and uniform nondegeneracy/C²/global curvature bounds. For rho_k=e^−2T_k and z=rho_k exp(t+i theta), |t|≤T_k, neck energy≤Ce^−2T_k. Every transformation with zero annular mean has finite pole in S_rho_k⊂global image, so cannot give the required closed smooth R3-valued immersion.
problems.counterevidence: The global Willmore hypothesis of the principal quantization theorem excludes the inserted open spherical pieces. The direct normalization conclusion of Theorem4.1 is weaker than the exact zero-mean condition and is not itself disproved by this example.
problems.impact: The asserted intermediate existence lemma feeding the core gauge/epsilon-regularity derivation fails under its expressly permitted local hypotheses. This is a concrete assumption mismatch, not merely a missing citation.
problems.correction: Strengthen to the appropriate global Willmore assumption and propagate scope, or replace exact zero mean by an approximate gauge and prove the necessary estimates; no such complete replacement is claimed.

check.independent_reasoning: Root checked the mean-zero inversion sphere and the two labelled spherical sheets whose complementary small surgery caps are disjoint. Their unchanged parts cover every possible pole, while T2#S2#S2 remains genus1 and compact smooth surgery gives uniform curvature bounds. The shrinking isothermal annulus has vanishing local Gauss energy and remains exactly Willmore. The expressly local hypotheses permit the inserted non-Willmore exterior; the global avoidance conclusion fails there. No globally Willmore main-theorem counterexample is claimed.
